text: {"bullets": [{"category": "growth", "point": "Real GDP growth is projected at 3.0 percent in 2024 and 4.3 percent in 2025, stabilizing at around 3.5 percent in the medium term.", "source_section": "Outlook And Risks"}, {"category": "inflation_monetary", "point": "CBS decreased the monetary policy rate to 1.75 percent in March 2024, maintaining an accommodative stance as inflation reached 0.6 percent in September and is projected to hit 2.5 percent by end-2024.", "source_section": "Context And Recent Developments"}, {"category": "financial_sector", "point": "Commercial banks remain well capitalized and liquid; NPLs fell from 8.2 percent at end-2023 to 7.2 percent in June 2024, though remaining elevated and concentrated in tourism.", "source_section": "Context And Recent Developments"}, {"category": "fiscal_debt", "point": "Public and publicly guaranteed debt is projected to reach 61.5 percent of GDP by end-2024, before declining to around 49 percent of GDP by 2029 supported by steady fiscal consolidation.", "source_section": "Public Debt Management and Government Financing"}, {"category": "external", "point": "The current account deficit will widen to 10.7 percent of GDP in 2024, but gross international reserves rose to $754 million by August 2024, equivalent to 3.5 months of import cover.", "source_section": "Context And Recent Developments"}, {"category": "risks", "point": "Downside risks stem from volatile global commodity prices, regional conflicts, slower growth in tourism source markets, climate-related natural disasters, and domestic credit concentration alongside elevated NPLs.", "source_section": "Outlook And Risks"}, {"category": "financial_sector", "point": "CBS is strengthening banking oversight through risk-based supervision and finalizing the draft Bank Resolution Bill, while amendments to the CBS Act require raising central bank capital to SR 550 million.", "source_section": "Financial Stability"}, {"category": "external", "point": "The Executive Board completed the third reviews under the EFF and RSF arrangements, approving about US$12.1 million in disbursements, including SDR 6.1 million under the EFF and SDR 3.1 million under the RSF.", "source_section": "Press Release"}, {"category": "structural_climate", "point": "Program performance remains good, but capacity constraints led to the rephasing and delay of RSF reform measures, while the National Climate Finance Strategy was adopted.", "source_section": "Program Performance"}]}
